note: Needs a two-level aggregate: group Users by post-owner, keep groups with COUNT(posts)>10, then average UpVotes and average Age across those groups in one 2-column row. ConQuer's GROUPED BY only produces a multi-row per-group list (a LIST query); a bare THE AVERAGE/THE COUNT aggregate produces a single scalar column and can filter via a correlated WHERE (the '!' correlation), but combining a bare aggregate with an explicit GROUPED BY sub-clause raised an internal compiler error ('node n3 has no anchor'), and there is no subquery/derived-table syntax to feed a grouped-and-filtered result back into an outer aggregate. The correlated-WHERE workaround (THE AVERAGE a IN User u has UserUpVotes a WHERE THE COUNT OF Post [has owner User: !u] > 10) does compile and is logically correct for ONE metric, but only yields a single column, not the two (up votes, age) columns needed side by side, and is also too slow to run in this session (no cheap pre-filter narrows the ~40,000 users before the ~92,000-row correlated Post scan per user, unlike Q672 where the UK-location filter cut it to 209 users). Concluded this composition is not expressible as a single well-formed, performant ConQuer query with the taught constructs.
